_purpose: Round 156 — Cura security sub-check rotation cursor. Records which surfaces Cura has audited recently so each night samples a rotating subset rather than scanning everything every fire. Mirrors tacitus/translation-audit-cursor.json shape (Round 136 precedent).
_owner: Cura — updated AFTER each nightly fire as the closing-move-atomic step of the Security sub-check

surfaces.surface: dashboard.html — input handlers (form fields, search, scanner inputs)
dashboard.html — cart import path (applyImportBundle / parseImportBundle / showImportPreview)
dashboard.html — localStorage write surfaces (schema validation gaps)
tools/* — safe_write surfaces (input validation on payload)
tools/best_practices_refresh.py (new — Round 155) — URL allowlist + response size cap

sampling_strategy: Each night Cura samples 2–3 surfaces from this list that have NOT been audited in the last rotation_cadence_days days, oldest-first. With 8 surfaces and 21-day cadence, each surface gets re-audited ~once every 21 days at the default sampling rate. After auditing a surface, Cura updates its `last_audited_at` field.
_owner_notes: Surfaces accumulate here as new attack surfaces emerge. User maintains; Cura uses (read+update). Adding a new surface requires the user to populate `lessons_pinned` so Cura has the relevant prior-art context.
